class View:
    def __init__(self):
        self.rows = []          # accepted rows (copy, immutable-like)
        self.notes = {}        # job_id -> note
        self.loading = False   # boolean exposed
        self.error = None      # clears on begin
        self.seq = 0           # monotonically increasing request id
        self._current_id = None  # latest begun request id (None if none)
    def begin(self, query):
        """Return monotonically increasing request id.
        Clears loading errors but keeps existing rows.
        """
        self.seq += 1
        id_ = self.seq
        self._current_id = id_
        self.loading = False
        self.error = None
        return id_
    def finish(self, request_id, rows):
        """Only the latest begun request can update rows, once.
        Older or duplicate replies return False.
        """
        if request_id != self._current_id:
            return False
        # copy accepted rows (deep copy list of rows)
        # spec says copy accepted rows; we store a copy
        self.rows = list(rows)  # simple copy; rows could be list
        # finish is called once for the current request
        self._current_id = None  # invalidate after successful finish
        return True
    def get_rows(self):
        """Expose rows (copy)."""
        # return a copy to avoid mutation
        return list(self.rows)
    def set_notes(self, job_id, note):
        """Preserve notes through all requests."""
        self.notes[job_id] = note
    def get_notes(self):
        """Expose notes (read-only copy)."""
        return dict(self.notes)
    def get_loading(self):
        """Expose loading boolean."""
        return self.loading
    def clear_error(self):
        """Clear loading errors on begin."""
        self.error = None
        self.loading = False

import view

def test_basic():
    v = view.View()
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    assert v.get_rows() == []
    assert v.get_notes() == {}
    # finish with same id succeeds
    rows1 = [1,2]
    ok = v.finish(id1, rows1)
    assert ok == True
    assert v.get_rows() == rows1
    # finish duplicate id should fail
    ok2 = v.finish(id1, rows1)  # second finish with same id should fail because id not current after first finish
    # after successful finish, _current_id should be None, so second finish returns False
    assert ok2 == False
    # new begin creates new id
    id2 = v.begin('q2')
    assert id2 > id1
    # finish with id2 succeeds
    rows2 = [3,4]
    ok3 = v.finish(id2, rows2)
    assert ok3 == True
    assert v.get_rows() == rows2  # rows updated to latest
    # finish with id1 (stale) should fail
    ok4 = v.finish(id1, rows1)
    assert ok4 == False

def test_preserve_notes():
    v = view.View()
    v.set_notes('job1', 'note1')
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    rows1 = [1]
    v.finish(id1, rows1)
    assert v.get_notes() == {'job1': 'note1'}
    # notes persist through begin/finish
    v.set_notes('job2', 'note2')
    id2 = v.begin('q2')
    rows2 = [2]
    v.finish(id2, rows2)
    assert v.get_notes() == {'job1': 'note1', 'job2': 'note2'}

def test_clear_error_and_keep_rows():
    v = view.View()
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    # finish not called yet, loading should be False
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    # set a dummy error? __init sets error None
    # begin clears error
    # simulate error by setting error then begin
    # but __init sets error None; we need to test that begin clears if error existed
    # we can directly set v.error = 'some error' before begin
    v.error = 'old error'
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    assert v.error is None
    # finish with id1 succeeds
    rows1 = [1]
    assert v.finish(id1, rows1) == True
    # start new request
    id2 = v.begin('q2')
    # loading False again
    # finish id2 succeeds
    rows2 = [2]
    assert v.finish(id2, rows2) == True
    # finish id1 (stale) fails
    assert v.finish(id1, rows1) == False

def test_expose_loading():
    v = view.View()
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    assert v.get_loading() == False  # begin sets loading False
    # after finish, loading stays False (spec says expose loading boolean)
    rows1 = [1]
    assert v.finish(id1, rows1) == True
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    # no explicit loading True state; spec says begin clears loading errors but keeps existing rows
    # so loading is just a flag that can be False when not in progress? We follow simple design.

def run_all():
    test_basic()
    test_preserve_notes()
    test_clear_error_and_keep_rows()
    test_expose_loading()
    print('All tests passed')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    run_all()
